articles.headline: Lip-Pickers run down the unanimous No. 1 on Monday night
articles.dek: Latina Lip-Pickers (6) trailed The Ripple Effect (1) by 13.14 going into Monday and won by 9.66. Davante Adams outscored Ripple Effect's entire Monday by himself.
body: The Ripple Effect went into Week 2 as the unanimous No. 1 in the power poll, holding every first-place vote in the league. They finished the week having scored 188.68 points, the second-highest total of the round, and lost.
Latina Lip-Pickers put up 198.34 — the highest score in the league this week — and did most of the damage after everyone else had stopped playing.

Going into Monday, Ripple Effect led 170.98 to 157.84. That is a 13.14-point cushion with one player left on each side, and the favourite had the safer name: Kyren Williams, a starting back in a normal workload, against a single wide receiver. Williams delivered, more or less, with 17.7. Ripple Effect also had Odell Beckham in the lineup, who finished on nought.
Davante Adams finished on 40.5. That is more than double what Ripple Effect got from their entire Monday, and it turned a 13.14-point deficit into a 9.66-point win by itself.

The margin is worth sitting with. Lip-Pickers won by 9.66 while starting a receiver who returned nothing of note in Rhamondre Stevenson (6.1) and a quarterback in Jacoby Brissett who managed 6.7. They won anyway, because CeeDee Lamb's 36.3 on Sunday kept the deficit inside one player's range and Adams covered the rest.

Ripple Effect, for their part, did very little wrong. Patrick Mahomes went for 36.38, Amon-Ra St. Brown for 35.7, Jonathan Taylor for 34.2 — three players over 34 points, and a total that would have beaten ten of the other eleven teams in the league. It beat the one that mattered by nothing at all.

Elsewhere the week was mostly orderly. Muffin Toppers handled Beasty Boys 187.86 to 166.76, which is the second week running that Beasty Boys have posted a respectable number and lost with it. THE REFUGEES beat The Phantom Troupe 175.32 to 159.70. Gods Favorite Jew took the week's ugliest fixture from Chinese Sweatshop, 125.46 to 111.06, in a game where the winner still finished below the league median.

The closest game of the week was The Tax over Parkers Dead Sons by 2.08 — 144.28 to 142.20 — which is the second time in two weeks that Parkers have lost a game they were one adequate performance from winning. They are 0-2 with a points total that would have them mid-table on a kinder schedule.

The median sat at 151.99, and six teams cleared it: Lip-Pickers, Ripple Effect, Muffin Toppers, THE REFUGEES, Beasty Boys and Phantom Troupe. The Tax won their head-to-head and still finished under it, which is the sort of week that looks fine in the standings and less fine in the points column.
Ballots for Week 3 open Tuesday at midnight. The unanimous No. 1 just lost to a team ranked sixth, and it will be interesting to see whether the league treats that as a result or as noise.

articles.headline: Week 2's two lowest scores meet on Monday night
articles.dek: Chinese Sweatshop (9) sit on 67.88. Gods Favorite Jew (11) sit on 100.26. Nobody else in the league is within eleven points of either of them.
body: Of the twelve scores posted in Week 2, the two smallest belong to the same matchup. Chinese Sweatshop have 67.88 points. Gods Favorite Jew have 100.26. The next worst in the league is Commercial Break on 111.96 — clear of Gods Favorite Jew by 11.7 and of Chinese Sweatshop by 44.08.
They play each other tonight, which is the only reason one of them is getting a win out of it.

Chinese Sweatshop trail by 32.38 and have two starters yet to register a point: Matthew Stafford and Isaiah Likely. That is the entire comeback. Applying the league's scoring to what is left, the projection has them finishing around 110.3 — Stafford for 26 and Likely for 16.4 — and that is the optimistic reading.

Because Gods Favorite Jew are still adding. Cam Skattebo and Blake Corum are yet to score, worth a projected 37.8 between them, which puts the other side somewhere near 138. The 32.38 is not a fixed target so much as a suggestion. Sweatshop need to outscore two players with two players, having already been outscored by a distance, and the maths gives them a 13 percent chance of managing it.

How Sweatshop got here is its own small catastrophe. DJ Moore finished on minus 0.1. Jayden Reed managed 0.9. DK Metcalf, the kind of name you start without thinking about it, returned 5.7. Tyler Shough's 28.38 is the only score on the sheet that would look normal on anyone else's team, and it is currently carrying 42 percent of the entire roster's output.

Gods Favorite Jew have the opposite problem, which is to say they have two good players and not much else. Brock Purdy's 36.08 and Geno Smith's 20.58 account for more than half their total. Bryce Lance contributed 1.3. It is not a performance anyone is putting on a highlight reel, but it has been enough to sit 32 points clear all weekend.
Neither side is going to trouble the league median of 151.06, so this is a straight fight over one win between two teams who are already looking up at everyone.

The poll, for what it is worth, sees no great difference between them either. Chinese Sweatshop (9) and Gods Favorite Jew (11) are separated by fifteen points and one spot in the standings, and both were ranked below Parkers Dead Sons (7), who are 0-2. A win tonight does not fix much. Losing it, on the other hand, would be the second-lowest score in the league losing to the third-lowest.
Monday night football, and the league will be watching for the wrong reasons.
